excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: <@602753420033785856> im curious why those rewards endpoints are on `/eth/v1/beacon/blocks` - is it possible to get the calculated rewards from just the block? I would have thought they'd be on `.../state`...

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: Fair point, they do require the state. The reason they're on `/blocks` is that they're about a single block

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: the `/attestations` namespace is maybe also a bit funny

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: if they make sense on /blocks im not against it... just feel like i kind of missed /lightclietn and dont want to stuff up again 😄

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: maybe they should all be grouped under `/eth/v1/beacon/rewards/{blocks,attestations,sync_committee_rewards}`

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: that might make more sense

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i guess we need more than just the block, and more than just the state, need a bit of a bunch of things

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so would still be based on a block id, but need a bunch of bits

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: yeah

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: so you thinking `/eth/v1/beacon/rewards/{block_id}/sync_committee_rewards`?

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
there are 3 APIs, I was thinking:

- `/eth/v1/beacon/rewards/blocks/{block_id}`
- `/eth/v1/beacon/rewards/sync_committee/{block_id}`
- `/eth/v1/beacon/rewards/attestations/{epoch}`

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: oh... so rewards/blocks/block_id is from block production...

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i can live with those 🙂

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: just thinking about them based on the sync committee change that's practically ready to merge

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: i can comment on the sync_committee one or you doing them already?

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: that might be good! it's your feedback after all 😁

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: I think both APIs are equally ready to merge

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: ok cool updating

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: ta for all the help on getting all these PRs done, its been a biggish job

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
I'd like to get a nod of agreement from the other client teams too, cc <@449019668296892420> <@688748669268132001> <@363800010518822915>

Context: For the EPF there are 3 people intending to work on implementing these APIs for all the clients. If nobody has any objections I'd like to merge the API PRs in the next week or so:

- Rewards for blocks and attestations: <https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/260>
- For sync committee messages: <https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/262>

thanks

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: thanks for leading the charge!

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: wdyt about keeping them in PR state until the client impls are done, in case there are performance (or other) considerations that come up during impl?

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: I'm not opposed to that. I was thinking we could always tweak things post-merge if issues arise or we want to add/remove things

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: the thinking being that there are lots of APIs in the `dev` branch of `beacon-APIs` that are not fully settled or implemented in clients

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: yeah, I find that messy - ie hard to know which api are "stable" (and thus reliable to base consumers on) - ie when cutting a release and we say we support API vx.y.z, it's hard to reason about these semi-stabilised parts -  maybe they can be marked experimental in the doc, then it's fine to merge early

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: yeah I'd be fine with marking them experimental

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: can mark experimental, I'd be fine with that, plus it's in dev atm...

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: It was mentioned in a team meeting the other day it'd be nice if we had a way of telling which clients have implemented which endpoints etc, which was done on keymanager, but that was a much smaller list... I'm not sure how feasible a list like that would be in beacon-apis... if anyone has feelings either way...

excerpts.author: kevinbogner
excerpts.content: How do we mark them as experimental? Add it to the endpoints description? Or even add 'experimental' as a tag?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: just make an 'Experimental' to put in the labels... will have a quick look

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
so in the 'tags' section, list 
```
tags:
    - Beacon
    - Rewards
    - Experimental
```

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: then when you run it you'll have an Experimental section, and any of your endpoints will list in that

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: also in the others... one option would be just list Experimental until we're happy with it

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: would probably be my preference, but I'm not strongly opinionated on that particular thing

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: <@1022784528579842079>  sorry that was all for you 🙂

excerpts.author: nc1234
excerpts.content: <@680234424037670912> <@602753420033785856> I've added the experimental tags for both PRs

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: Thanks for that, we'll take another look today

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
The only other observation on those rewards apis is probably just something to keep in mind - previously with id as a query parameter we've hit limits that we wouldn't have had a problem with if it were a POST and a list supplied in the body. this was a problem with validators where people wanted to specify huge numbers of validators in a single query, as some services were only allowing short urls...
I'm not sure how these are intended to be used, but if it's likely that people may want large numbers of validator id's in a single url (or lots of pubkeys), then it's worth thinking through <@602753420033785856> 
This is late feedback, you've probably talked about it already but i feel it's at least worth mentioning 🙂

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: happy to run with them as they stand, just putting it out there

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: ah yeah, that isn't something we'd discussed actually

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: I'm inclined to say we _should_ go ahead with the POST actually

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: as the response data is likely to be massive and having to fetch the whole validator set once you go past the URL length limit would be a pain
